question: is the committed source evidence the same bytes the upstream archives contain, not merely files with the right names

three_levels.claim: every claim locator file digest and the excerpt hash at the recorded line range
three_levels.member: the archive accepted only on a digest match before anything is read from it
three_levels.byte: each committed file compared byte for byte with the same member extracted from the re-fetched archive

why: an archive digest proves the archive; it does not prove that the file in the repository is the file that came out of it
incomplete_record_note: one record is a versioned PDF with no TeX members, so it has no file list to compare and is reported as incomplete rather than counted as verified
coverage_limit: all 38 source receipt files have now been checked at byte level; the limit is that a re-fetch depends on the upstream service continuing to serve those exact versions

full_coverage_run.reading: every committed source file that has an archive member is byte identical to that member, fetched fresh and accepted only on a digest match

status_naming_correction.issue: a record served as a versioned PDF was reported as NOT_AN_ARCHIVE, which reads like a failure although its digest had already been verified
status_naming_correction.remedy: that case now reports DIGEST_VERIFIED_NO_MEMBERS, which states what was established and what was not

staleness_contract: this receipt records the digest of the claim locator file it was run against; when that file changes the recorded result no longer applies and the gate reports it as stale
